explanation: I found no Mathlib theorem that states this result. The statement says: if multiplication by n is surjective on A and α : A →+ B vanishes on its kernel, then there is a β with β(n•Q) = α Q and α P = n • β P. The first clause is the standard factorisation through a surjective homomorphism. Mathlib provides that only as a construction, `AddMonoidHom.liftOfRightInverse` / `liftOfRightInverseAux` in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean, or via `QuotientAddGroup.lift`. Using it here would require building a right inverse of `zsmulAddGroupHom n`, translating the kernel hypothesis, and then proving the extra clause α P = n • β P separately. That takes more than two lines of glue. I grepped for existence-style factorisation and lift lemmas (`exists_*lift`, `*factor*Surjective`) in Mathlib/Algebra/Group and found no statement of this shape.
